findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Sausage croissants, Lunchables and snack packs in the standing display cooler as you enter the facility are observed with internal temperatures of 45.3F. The PIC was shown and discarded the TCS foods in this cooler to correct the immediate violation. The cooler functioning correctly is being handled on line item #33 of this report. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at safe temperatures throughout storage until service.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY.

The bleach being used for the three part sink is a low-splash variation that is not intended for food service/contact. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace prior to the follow-up. The normal follow-up time frame is being pushed back to coincide with the other follow ups on this report. Ensure that all sanitizers used on food contact surfaces are intended for for food contact surfaces in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The cooler used for storage of sausage, cheese and other proteins is holding foods at 45.3F. The PIC was consulted and instructed to have the cooler repaired prior to the follow-up.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Both CL and Quat based sanitizers are available in the facility. Test strips are only available for the CL sanitizer during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to acquired test strips for both sanitizers used in the facility prior to the follow-up.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. P (C) PACKAGED Food shall be properly labeled.

1) The PIC could not show that the freeze dried items in the store are received from a retailer. They stated that they are primarily received from Nassau and repackaged in store for sale. Ensure that sourcing is available for all foods. The PIC indicated that they could send the inspector a copy of an invoice with the items on it when her husband becomes available as he is the one that mostly does the ordering. 2) The labels of these items need some indication of being repackaged from another company. Currently the labels indicate the food and the ingredients that are used to produce them only. The PIC pulled down the freeze dries items until the questions can be resolved.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink next to the three part sink does not have paper towels available during this inspection. Paper towels were provided during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

During this inspection the employees were unable to show where a sanitizer was available for making a solution effective for use on food contact surfaces. A sanitizer should be available for use at the follow up in two weeks.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

The employee in the facility at the start of this inspection indicated that they did not have a food handler certification at all. The employee that arrived part of the way through the inspection to relieve her also did not have a food handler certification available for observation. Ensure that all food handlers at the facility have a food handler certification prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Reporting agreements are not on file. Employee was not aware of any reporting agreement. Inspector provided facility with a blank reporting agreement to be copied and signed by all employees.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Vomit/diarrhea clean up policy could not be provided during inspection. Inspector will provide facility with a norovirus clean up policy to be kept on file for reference in the event of vomit or diarrhea in the facility.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Spray bottle of blue liquid observed under the cashier counter without a label indicating contents. CORRECTED- Discussed with employee, who indicated that the liquid is window cleaner. Employee labeled bottle.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Food handler certificates could not be provided for review during inspection. Ensure all employees who handle food (candy) or utensils complete food handler training. Keep certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]
